description: Analysis of IC3/PDR finite-theory anchoring: precision enrichment vs convergence. Documents that finite theories provide bug class coverage, not convergence acceleration.

ablation_analysis.key_observation: Frame counts are IDENTICAL between 5-theory and 2-theory across all 32 benchmarks (avg delta = 0.0). All 32/32 verdicts agree.
ablation_analysis.convergence_impact: NONE — finite theories do not affect convergence
ablation_analysis.correct_framing: Finite theories (T_device, T_phase, T_perm) provide PRECISION ENRICHMENT, not convergence acceleration. They expand the set of bug classes that can be detected, without changing the frame structure or convergence properties of IC3/PDR.

examples.name: device_transfer_missing
examples.explanation: Shapes match (256→128→64) so T_shape says SAFE. But if fc1 is on GPU and fc2 on CPU, runtime crashes. T_device catches this.

examples.name: device_mixed_gpu_cpu
examples.explanation: Shape-wise correct (Conv2d→GlobalAvgPool→Linear). Device bug only manifests when conv is on cuda:0, fc on cpu.

examples.name: dropout_eval_semantic
examples.explanation: Shapes match in both train and eval. But the model behaves differently: in train, dropout scales outputs by 2x; in eval, it's identity. T_phase flags phase-dependent behavior.

examples.name: batchnorm_eval_stats
examples.explanation: Shapes correct. But BatchNorm behavior differs between train (batch statistics) and eval (running statistics). T_phase enriches the analysis with this distinction.

examples.name: transpose_dim_swap
examples.explanation: After fc1, shape is (batch, seq, 128). Transpose swaps seq↔128. fc2 expects 128 but gets seq. Both T_shape and T_perm can catch this, but T_perm provides richer diagnostic about which axes swapped.

bugs_found.message: self.fc2: input last dim is 20, but nn.Linear expects in_features=30
self.conv2: input channel dim is 16, but nn.Conv2d expects in_channels=32
self.dec2: input last dim is 128, but nn.Linear expects in_features=256

examples.name: linear_chain_safe
examples.explanation: No bugs to catch. Both theories correctly say SAFE.

examples.name: conv_chain_safe
examples.explanation: No bugs to catch. Both theories correctly say SAFE.

examples.name: mlp_safe
examples.explanation: No bugs to catch. Both theories correctly say SAFE.

timing.conclusion: The 5-theory configuration adds ~12ms average overhead (~52% relative) but this is acceptable: all benchmarks complete in <110ms. The cost buys coverage of 3 additional bug classes.

finding: Finite theories (T_device, T_phase, T_perm) provide PRECISION ENRICHMENT, not convergence acceleration. Frame counts are identical with and without these theories across all tested benchmarks. The value of the 5-theory configuration is strictly in expanding bug class coverage: 2 device bugs, 2 phase-sensitive behaviors, and 0 permutation bugs that 2-theory would miss. Total precision gain: 4 additional bugs caught.

correct_framing.wrong: Finite theories accelerate IC3/PDR convergence via finite-domain anchoring of the frame sequence.
correct_framing.right: Finite theories enrich IC3/PDR PRECISION by expanding the set of detectable bug classes from shape-only to shape+device+phase+permutation. Convergence is unaffected.
